column1: # Reference panel template for nf-helminth-amplicon
# Tab-separated, nine columns, header required. Lines starting with # are
# ignored, so these notes can stay in the file. Empty fields are genuinely
# empty - do not write NA or "." .
# Validate the panel on its own while you build it, before a samplesheet exists:
#   python3 bin/preflight.py --reference my_panel.tsv \
#       --assay assets/assay/ampseq_helminth.json --outdir check
# COLUMNS
#   seq_id        unique, filesystem-safe (letters, digits, . _ -)
#   locus         required for target/control/quant; groups the panel
#   type          target | control | quant | vector
#   purpose       speciation | variants | speciation,variants | (blank)
#                 What the reference is FOR, as opposed to what it is.
#                 Blank means speciation, so panels written before this
#                 column existed behave unchanged.
#                 This matters even with no variant calling: rel_abundance
#                 divides by total target reads, so a second locus added
#                 without marking it would count every species twice, with a
#                 denominator mixing loci at different copy numbers.
#                 Not exclusive - a single-copy locus can serve both, since
#                 its copy number does not vary between species the way a
#                 multi-copy marker's does. Controls inherit from their
#                 parent; quants and vectors take neither.
#   taxon         optional; blank falls back to seq_id. Give every haplotype
#                 of one species the SAME taxon so counts aggregate
#   parent_id     required for control; must name a target at the same locus
#   default_conc  required for quant; numeric, > 0
#   conc_units    required for quant, e.g. copies_per_rxn. An implicit unit
#                 is how a copy number becomes uninterpretable later
#   corr_factor   optional amplification-efficiency multiplier, relative to
#                 the quant standards. BLANK defaults to 1.0.
#                 The default is the honest arithmetic either way - dividing
#                 by 1 is what "no correction" already did - but the results
#                 record corr_factor_source as "panel" or "default", because
#                 measured-and-found-to-be-unity and assumed-to-be-unity are
#                 the same number backed by different evidence.
#                 With everything at the default, copy numbers are relative
#                 to the standards' efficiency rather than corrected to it.
#                 That compares samples with each other correctly; it does
#                 not compare species with each other, since a reference
#                 that amplifies twice as well reads twice as abundant.
#   sequence      uppercase IUPAC, no gaps, FULL AMPLICON including the
#                 primer-binding sites
# SEQUENCES
#   Use the same extent for every entry. Mixing insert-only and full-amplicon
#   sequences biases competitive assignment toward the longer ones, for
#   reasons that have nothing to do with which is actually present.
# CONTROLS
#   Build each control as its parent sequence with the tag inserted:
#       control = parent[:position] + TGGTCAATTTCAAGAGAT + parent[position:]
#   Pre-flight recovers the tag and its position by aligning control to
#   parent, and will refuse a control whose insertion is not the expected tag.
# WHAT WILL BE REJECTED
#   - two entries with identical sequences (competitive assignment cannot
#     separate them, so this is an error rather than a warning)
#   - a control with no parent_id, or one naming a different locus
#   - a quant missing default_conc or conc_units
#   - the tag occurring inside a target sequence
#   - non-IUPAC characters, or gaps
seq_id
# --- targets: one row per haplotype, same taxon to aggregate -------------
Nam_ITS2_h1
Nam_ITS2_h2
Asc_ITS2_h1
Tri_ITS2_h1
Nam_ITS2_h1_ctrl
Asc_ITS2_h1_ctrl
Tri_ITS2_h1_ctrl
# --- quantification standards, two orders of magnitude apart -------------
QUANT_hi
QUANT_lo
# --- optional: plasmid backbone as a non-specific amplification sensor ---
pUC19_bb
